title: Projection right tensor action at integral coefficients
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, an integer $n\ge1$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $S$ be a six-functor datum at these coefficients [def-sf-datum], with the specified operation and comparison data [def-fix-six-functor-datum].

Work at $\Lambda=R$ in the bounded constructible derived-complete integral categories $D^b_c(T,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes and supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ with $j$ open, $p$ proper and $pj=f$. Write $F=Rf_!^c$, $U=Lf^*$, and $P(K,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c:FK\otimes L\to F(K\otimes UL)$ for the datum's actual compactification projection, namely the proper counit projection followed by the open tensor comparison [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates, def-exchange-projection]. Write $a_T(A,B,C):(A\otimes B)\otimes C\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes(B\otimes C)$ for the canonical tensor associator conjugated by the datum's tensor normalization, and $\mu_f(L,N):U(L\otimes N)\xrightarrow{\sim}UL\otimes UN$ for the canonical normalized tensor-pullback comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Then, for every $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L,N\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, with no additional finite-Tor restriction on these inputs,
$$\begin{aligned}
P(K\otimes UL,N)\circ(P(K,L)\otimes1_N)
={}&F\bigl(a_X(K,UL,UN)^{-1}\bigr)\circ F(1_K\otimes\mu_f(L,N))\\
&\circ P(K,L\otimes N)\circ a_Y(FK,L,N).
\end{aligned}$$
Both sides are morphisms $(FK\otimes L)\otimes N\to F((K\otimes UL)\otimes UN)$. The two final images under $F$ are separate composites. All tensors, associators and pullbacks are the specified completed integral, rationalized, or common-stage operations, according to the coefficient stage. This is an equality of projection maps without an extra invertibility hypothesis. Taking $N$ to be the degree-zero constant quotient $(\Lambda/J)_Y$ for an ideal $J\subseteq\Lambda$ gives reduction inside the original coefficient category; $UN$ is its canonical pulled-back coefficient object. The assertion is for arbitrary $N$, not only constant quotients.

Verbatim retained old parent argument, in source order:
For coefficients, [prop-sf-pf-reduction] supplies the finite reduction square on the finite-Tor domains. At field stages use the integral representatives, rationalization and common-stage comparisons of [thm-sf-pf-field]. The (A5) comparisons [def-sf-datum] and primitive-map data [def-exchange-projection] satisfy the intertwining and cocycle hypotheses of [lem-sf-pf-coefficient-realization-transport]. It carries the proved equal composites and their unit identifications to the specified coefficient/site maps; its cocycles give coefficient naturality. [thm-sf-pf-proetale] identifies the realized projection with the same proper counit projection followed by the open tensor map. Integral commutativity was proved directly in step 2; fields use chosen integral representatives, never reduction of field objects. For the finite all-ideal clause, [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates] gives the actual component and its recorded source and target realization comparisons. Conjugate by these comparisons and cancel the inverse/hom composites; the fully faithful preimage equation for the realization equivalence identifies the arrow with fixedComponent. Its tensor-coordinate evaluation is the same canonical proper/open projection. Apply the expanded general coefficient-category compactification tensor-action identity [lem-sf-projection-tensor-coordinate-action], proved from the existing generic library calculation in [lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws] with third input the degree-zero constant quotient A/J. Functorial preservation of composition separates the pullback tensor comparison and the inverse target associator. The quotient is arbitrary; no perfectness or flatness assumption is imposed. The remaining coefficient clauses retain the preceding plan.

from.place: Final finite-reduction clause: tensor-action equation at the integral coefficient stage

proof.text: First check the domain of the completion calculation. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], every integral bounded constructible input has uniformly finite-Tor reductions; this applies to K,L,N, not merely to a chosen finite-Tor subcategory. Apply [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] repeatedly to the pullbacks and binary/triple tensors in the two routes. Apply [lem-fix-compactification-completed-realization] to every source input of F: its hidden j_! intermediate and its proper direct-image output are derived-complete constructible. The system intermediates are the strict towers, not reductions of these outputs, so identify them. For the hidden open intermediate, J_j(RK) has levels j_!K_n, which are the reductions of j_!K by the open tensor isomorphism gamma of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] with N=(A_n)_{\overline X}. For the proper output, S_pJ_j(RK) has levels Rp_{*,n}j_!K_n; since every K_n has Tor amplitude in one interval [a,b], [lem-coef-compact-support-normalized-realization] for the compactification c=(j,p) says this tower is a normalized DVR tower. By [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] its levels are the reductions of its total limit, which is Rp_{*,R}j_!K by the isomorphism d_c above. Applying the residue-Tor result to these complete constructible outputs therefore gives uniform Tor bounds and bounded constructible cohomology for the system intermediates themselves. Thus all finitely many intermediate objects satisfy the uniform bounds of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. The finite inputs have compatible etale origins by the equivalence in [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]: choose its quasi-inverse on the entire reduction diagram, so transition maps and their relations are retained, rather than choosing unrelated origins. Boundedness gives bounded-below origins. These checks require no separated structure morphism for X or Y.

proof.text: Work before total inverse limit in the derived categories of strict semilinear coefficient systems supplied by [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Their simultaneous ringed-diagram-site models let us use the ordinary ringed derived calculation. Put P=P_p, Q=P_j, R=S_p, J=J_j and H=RJ. Write A,B,C for the coherent reductions of K,L,N. Tensor and pullback constraints are the canonical total-complex constraints. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], P,Q are strong monoidal, and the comparison P_f -> QP is monoidal. The normalization in [def-sfb-ringed-projection-coherence-data] fixes the associator used in the next step as the total-complex reassociation, rather than an arbitrary associator. Denote by pi the counit-defined projection for P adjoint to R, and by delta the open tensor map for J adjoint to Q. The compactification projection in systems is R(delta_{A,PB}) pi_{JA,B}, followed by the image of the inverse pullback compositor, exactly as in [def-exchange-projection].

source.place: Proper counit mate and open tensor factors; canonical tensor reassociations

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-associativity] to the proper ringed-diagram-site morphism p and its canonical tensor models. Its projection is pi, since both are the transpose of (epsilon tensor 1) mu_p. Its normalized TensorConstraints are the constraints fixed in step 2. Precompose its displayed equality by alpha_Y(RM,B,C); the inverse source associator cancels. The result, in right-to-left composition, is
pi_{M tensor PB,C}(pi_{M,B} tensor 1_C)
=R(alpha^{-1}_{M,PB,PC}) R(1_M tensor mu_p(B,C)) pi_{M,B tensor C} alpha_Y(RM,B,C).
This holds for arbitrary system objects, so in particular for M=JA. It is an equality of counit-defined maps and does not use their invertibility.

source.place: Proper factor: transpose the two tensor-action routes through the same adjunction

proof.text:
For the open factor, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] applies on the ringed diagram site with its actual coefficient transitions. It identifies delta^{-1}_{A,B} with the J adjoint to Q transpose of mu_j^{-1}(v_A tensor 1). Hence it is exactly kappa of [lem-pur-unit-adjunct-tensor-action]. Invert that node's first equation (every kappa here is invertible by the open normalization), obtaining
delta_{A tensor QB,C}(delta_{A,B} tensor 1_C)
=J(alpha^{-1}_{A,QB,QC}) J(1_A tensor mu_j(B,C)) delta_{A,B tensor C} alpha(JA,B,C).
Indeed inversion reverses the two kappa factors, and the inverse of J((1 tensor mu_j^{-1}) alpha) is J(alpha^{-1}(1 tensor mu_j)). Thus this is the required open action equation with the canonical maps, including their unit normalization.

source.place: Open factor: unit-normalized tensor comparison and its two-factor action equation

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-composite-relative-tensor-action] with its (R,P,pi) equal to the proper factor and its (J,Q,delta) equal to the open factor. Steps 3 and 4 supply exactly its two hypotheses, on the same system tensor categories. It gives the action law for tau_{A,B}=R(delta_{A,PB}) pi_{JA,B} and pullback QP. Its explicit expansion uses naturality of pi to move R(delta) through the next projection, so no interchange between the two factors is left implicit. Replace QP by P_f via the canonical inverse-image compositor. The monoidality equation of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] identifies mu_{QP}=mu_j P_j(mu_p) with mu_f under this compositor; naturality inserts the same compositor in tau and tau at A tensor P_f B. Therefore the resulting equality is the desired compactification action equation in the derived system category, including the canonical pullback-composition factors.

proof.text: Apply the total-limit functor to step 5's equality as an equality in the derived system category. Use the c_V of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] for its source, target, and every intermediate expression. That theorem intertwines each proper/open projection constituent, unit, counit, tensor/pullback comparison and its whiskering by these expressions. For the associators use [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], which identifies completed reassociation with the limit of the whole system reassociation, with the actual reduction-limit counits. The comparison mu_f is precisely [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], defined from that strict tensor comparison with its completion units. For each constituent m:V->W the comparison equation is c_W L(m)=m_int c_V. Substitution in each composite cancels each adjacent c_V^{-1}c_V, leaving the same c_source and c_target on the two sides. Cancel these isomorphisms. This proves equality of the completed integral composites themselves; finite evaluation is never used to detect equality of morphisms.
